figures.caption: Table 5: FFN zero ablation: forecasting degradation when post-GELU activations are replaced with zeros during inference. The FFN is functionally active across the large majority of settings, with degradation most pronounced on higher-dimensional datasets.

Table 3: SAE sparsity calibration: average L0 (active latents per token) across λ values, averaged over all prediction horizons. Both dictionary sizes respond smoothly to reduced sparsity pressure, confirming the SAE instrument is properly calibrated.

Table 4: Forecasting performance comparison between our single-layer model (unified configuration, no per-dataset tuning) and the published PatchTST/42 [Nie et al., 2023] (3 layers, per-dataset tuning). Exchange is excluded as it was not evaluated in the original PatchTST paper.
